categories.name: It works
categories.notes: Build OK (0 errors; the 10 warnings are the scaffold's ImageSharp NU190x advisories, not model-introduced). / returns 200 as the blog front page and lists both posts as cards with a cropped listing image, title, date and excerpt; links work. Both posts render all 4 blocks (rich text, image with credit caption, rich text, quote) with no 'Could not render component'. Images are the provided Unsplash photos imported into a Blog media folder and served via signed GetCropUrl URLs (4/4 load). Domain '/' sits on the front page (not WWW); all pages published.

categories.name: Content modeling
categories.notes: richTextBlock, imageBlock, quoteBlock are elements in Blocks; blogFrontPage and blogPost are documents in Pages. One custom 'Blog Block Grid' (12 columns, all three blocks) used as body on both page types. siteRoot -> blogFrontPage -> blogPost allowed children are tight, templates assigned as default, camelCase aliases. Post metadata (publishDate, excerpt, listingImage) are real properties. No compositions, no duplicate or orphaned types/data types (one imported photo, circuit-board, is unused, which is harmless).

categories.name: Code architecture & conventions
categories.notes: Both page views render with Html.GetBlockGridHtmlAsync(Model, "body"); scaffold blockgrid partials untouched. Three alias-named adapters in Views/Partials/blockgrid/Components/ take BlockGridItem<T>, map to records in Models/Blocks/ and call Component.InvokeAsync with no markup. Three *ViewComponent classes with plain Views/Shared/Components/{RichText,Image,Quote}/Default.cshtml. Program.cs/appsettings.json untouched, no migrations, GetCropUrl and Url() used, Tailwind built to wwwroot/dist/site.css. Full HTML shell in each view with Layout = null is what the prompt prescribed (no shared layout in scaffold). Trivial: the post's back link is hard-coded to '/'.

categories.name: Content & presentation
categories.notes: Two on-topic, accurate posts ('MCP Turns Tools Into Teammates', 'One Protocol, Every Assistant') covering the integration tax, the tools/resources/prompts contract, JSON-RPC over stdio/HTTP, capability negotiation and the N×M problem, each spread over 4 blocks with relevant abstract network photos and pull quotes. They are on the short side (about 4 paragraphs, ~220 words each), and part of post 1 is about building this site. Presentation is clean: dark header, two-column card grid with images, readable max-w-3xl post column with spaced paragraphs, rounded image with caption and an indigo pull quote.

categories.name: Process & honesty
categories.notes: All schema/content via the two Umbraco MCP servers (48 MCP calls, no Management API/DB/browser/migration/uSync use, no memory or out-of-folder access). Followed the step order, except it skipped the recipe's 'siteRoot allows blogFrontPage' update in step 3 and only made it after create-page failed (-0.5). publish-page with includeDescendants was cancelled by the tool, so it published the pages one by one; that was a reasonable workaround and it disclosed it. The final report is accurate and discloses both problems and the ViewComponent naming fix.

summary: A clean, fully working MCP-built blog: three well-formed blocks on one custom block grid, a front page of image/date/excerpt cards and two published posts, rendered through the prescribed adapter -> plain model -> ViewComponent pipeline with polished Tailwind styling. The only blemishes are fairly short posts and a skipped siteRoot allowed-children step that it fixed reactively.
strengths: All 43 automated checks pass; build clean apart from the scaffold's package advisories.
Textbook block pipeline: alias-named adapters, records in Models/Blocks, one ViewComponent per block, GetBlockGridHtmlAsync on both pages.
Correct, tight schema: right folders, allowed children, real post metadata, one custom block grid.
Provided Unsplash photos imported to a Blog media folder, served via signed GetCropUrl, with photographer credits as captions.
Polished, readable design; fast (4:12) run with an honest report.

issues.text: Posts are short (~4 paragraphs, ~220 words each); part of /mcp-turns-tools-into-teammates/ is about building this site rather than MCP in general.
Skipped the recipe's siteRoot -> blogFrontPage allowed-children update in step 3; only fixed it after create-page failed with 'Operation not permitted' (disclosed in the report).
Views/blogPost.cshtml hard-codes the back link to '/' instead of linking to the parent page's Url().
